title: Pullback is t-exact for the standard constructible t-structures
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, with the rationalized category $D^b_c(-,E)$ and the common-stage category $D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $h:W\to X$ be a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $Lh^*:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$ be the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use on both sides the standard pair [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], its constructible heart $\Sh_c(-,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-constructible-heart] and the cohomology functors $\mathcal H^j$ [prop-constructible-truncations].

Then $Lh^*$ is $t$-exact: $Lh^*D^{\le0}_c(X,\Lambda)\subset D^{\le0}_c(W,\Lambda)$ and $Lh^*D^{\ge0}_c(X,\Lambda)\subset D^{\ge0}_c(W,\Lambda)$. Consequently $Lh^*$ restricts to an exact functor $\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)\to\Sh_c(W,\Lambda)$, and for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $j\in\mathbf Z$ the truncation maps induce a natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)\cong Lh^*\mathcal H^j(K)$. In particular, for a geometric point $\bar x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and the point-fibre functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal H^j(K))\cong\mathrm H^j(\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*K))$, and for $\mathcal F\in\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)$ the complex $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal F)$ is concentrated in degree zero. At $\Qlb$ all these maps are the scalar extensions of the corresponding maps at a common finite coefficient-field stage.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3) (constructible $\mathcal O_E$-complexes are the bounded ones with constructible cohomology sheaves, locally $\Lambda\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E,X}$ on strata), Remark 6.8.15 ($f^*K=f^*_{\mathrm{naive}}K\otimes_{f^*_{\mathrm{naive}}\Lambda_X}\Lambda_Y$), and Proposition 6.8.14(2) for rationalization; the t-exactness is the agent's reading of these places.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, $A_n=R/\pi^n$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$. First work integrally. The schemes $X,W$ are Noetherian and finite-dimensional: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose one-point space is quasi-compact and whose field coordinate ring is Noetherian. Also $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] applies to exactly the integral category used here, including its uniform reduction bounds. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$, [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](1) ensures $Lh^*K\in D^b_c(W,R)$ with the specified finite reductions. We will prove that any cohomological interval $[a,b]$ for $K$ is also an interval for $Lh^*K$.

Choose the finite constructible locally closed stratification $i_\alpha:S_\alpha\to X$ and pro-etale covers $v_{\alpha t}:V_{\alpha t}\to S_\alpha$ in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization](ii). Write $K|_{V_{\alpha t}}\cong B_{V_{\alpha t}}\otimes_R P_{\alpha t}^\bullet$, with $P^\bullet$ bounded finite projective. Restrictions here are ordinary exact inverse images, and they agree with the item's integral pullback. By [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] the integral pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] along any morphism is naturally isomorphic to the strict-tower completed pullback, compatibly with the finite reductions; for immersions [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison] identifies the latter with the exact ordinary inverse image. For $v_{\alpha t}$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $V_{\alpha t,\mathrm{proet}}$ with the localized site and [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction](3) identifies the module inverse image $v_{\alpha t}^*$ with restriction to it, which is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact]. Restriction evaluates a sheaf on the same objects, so it preserves the sectionwise products of [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and the inverse limit defining $B$. Applying it to both coordinates of the Roos cone in [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] therefore also commutes with completed pullback. In particular these restrictions commute with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]; hence $K|_{V_{\alpha t}}$ still has cohomology only in $[a,b]$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Lemma 6.5.8 and Remark 6.5.10; replete inverse-limit model of §3.1

proof.text:
Here is the scalar-model calculation needed for these chosen $P^\bullet$. Its completed-coefficient representative is bounded and termwise projective, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For a morphism $g:V'\to V$, the reduction of $B_V\otimes_RP^\bullet$ is $(A_n)_V\otimes_RP^\bullet$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction]. Its finite pullback is $(A_n)_{V'}\otimes_RP^\bullet$: the constant-section comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] preserves each scalar matrix, and the finite module pullback is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Consequently the defining reduction-tower formula in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] gives
$$Lg^*(B_V\otimes_RP^\bullet)\cong R\varprojlim_n((A_n)_{V'}\otimes_RP^\bullet)\cong B_{V'}\otimes_RP^\bullet.$$
For the last equality, each projective term is a summand of a finite free module. The tower of that term has epimorphic transitions, so [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] computes its derived limit as its ordinary limit. Finite sums and projectors commute with the limit, and the exact functor $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] commutes with the finitely many cones constructing the bounded complex. Thus the same differential matrices occur after the limit. All maps used are the constant-section and quotient maps, so this calculation respects their transitions.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), finite perfect scalar models; Lemma 6.5.8; §3.1; Stacks Tag 093M (sites-modules.tex, lemma-completion-flat)

proof.text:
Base change the chosen strata and covers to $W$. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification], $S'_\alpha=W\times_XS_\alpha\to W$ is a finite stratification; its strata are constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. The base changes $V'_{\alpha t}=W\times_XV_{\alpha t}\to S'_\alpha$ cover in the pro-etale topology, by its base-change-stable covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $g_{\alpha t}:V'_{\alpha t}\to V_{\alpha t}$ be the projection. The two factorizations of $V'_{\alpha t}\to X$, together with the composition comparison [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], identify
$$(Lh^*K)|_{V'_{\alpha t}}\cong Lg_{\alpha t}^*(K|_{V_{\alpha t}})\cong B_{V'_{\alpha t}}\otimes_RP_{\alpha t}^\bullet.$$
The first isomorphism uses the exact immersion and site restrictions just established in Step 2; the second is Step 3. Empty base-changed strata contribute no condition. This uses actual fibre-product strata and their projection morphisms.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, pullback of its stratified models; Lemma 6.5.9

proof.text:
Fix one of the models in Step 4, abbreviating it by $P^\bullet$ on $V$, and put $N^j=H^j(P^\bullet)$. The constant-sheaf functor $M\mapsto\underline M$ is exact, since it is sectionwise exact by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties](1), so $H^j(\underline{P^\bullet})=\underline{N^j}$; tensoring with $B_T$ is exact by flatness of $B_T$ over the constant ring $R$ in [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to these two exact functors gives
$$H^j(B_T\otimes_RP^\bullet)=B_T\otimes_R\underline{N^j}_T\quad(T=V,V').$$
For $j\notin[a,b]$ the expression at $V$ is zero by Step 2. Its underived ringed pullback along $g:V'\to V$ is $B_{V'}\otimes_R\underline{N^j}_{V'}$: on balanced tensors the identification is $b'\otimes(b\otimes n)\mapsto b'g^\sharp(b)\otimes n$, with inverse $b'\otimes n\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes n)$. Constant sheaves pull back to the same constant module; this follows by applying the constant functor and inverse image to a presentation, both being left adjoints, or directly from their constant-section universal property [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Underived pullback sends the zero module to zero. Therefore the expression at $V'$ is zero as well. This only uses scalar flatness over $R$, and does not require flatness of $B_{V'}$ over $g^{-1}B_V$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite scalar models; Stacks Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat

proof.text: The exact restrictions to $S'_\alpha$ and $V'_{\alpha t}$ commute with cohomology as in Step 2. For $j\notin[a,b]$, Steps 4-5 show that every such restriction of $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)$ vanishes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] on the Noetherian scheme $W$ to its underlying abelian sheaf: $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)=0$. Thus integral pullback preserves every cohomological interval $[a,b]$. In particular if $K$ is in the integral nonpositive half, choose a lower bound $a$ and take $b=0$; if it is in the nonnegative half choose an upper bound $b$ and take $a=0$. The integral standard classes in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] are therefore preserved. No restriction is imposed on the geometric fibres of $h$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), detection on a finite stratification

proof.text: Pass to $E$. Integral pullback is $R$-linear by its termwise scalar action. By [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] it is naturally isomorphic on derived complete objects, in particular on $D^b_c$, to the strict-tower completed pullback, which preserves shifts and distinguished triangles of complete objects by [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles]; transporting that shift comparison along the natural isomorphism, the integral pullback is exact on $D^b_c(X,R)\to D^b_c(W,R)$. Its extension on fractions is precisely the rational pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] shows it is again exact. An object in either rational standard half is, by [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], isomorphic after rationalization to an integral object in that half. Applying $Lh^*$ to this isomorphism and using Step 6 puts its image in the same rational half. This proves both required inclusions for $E$. The argument uses the isomorphism closures in the definition, and does not infer an integral bound from an arbitrary rational representative.

At $\Qlb$, use the objects $(F,M)$ and common-stage morphisms of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Pullback sends this object to $(F,Lh_F^*M)$, and acts on arrows by the scalar-extension comparison specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. An object of either standard half is isomorphic to such a pair with $M$ in that half at a finite field $F$, by [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. Step 7, applied to $F$, sends it into the required half. The functor is exact: a distinguished triangle has a representative at one common finite field, and its image there is distinguished by Step 7, hence also in the pair category. This proves t-exactness at $\Qlb$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and the common-stage convention; Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: By [prop-constructible-truncations], both standard pairs are bounded t-structures. Steps 7-8 and shift compatibility give preservation of both halves at every integer. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to the exact functor $Lh^*$. Its unique comparisons commute with the canonical truncation maps, hence their composite and the shift comparison give the stated natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)\cong Lh^*\mathcal H^j(K)$. T-exactness also sends the intersection of the two halves into their intersection, the hearts of [def-weil-constructible-heart]. A short exact heart sequence gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4); its image is a distinguished triangle with all vertices in the target heart, hence is a short exact sequence by the same clause. The heart functor is therefore exact.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11 and Proposition 6.8.14; BBD 1.3.3-1.3.6 for the generic truncation/heart argument

proof.text: These comparisons respect finite coefficient extension. Indeed [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] supplies the natural pullback comparison and its tower compatibility, while [prop-constructible-truncations] gives the corresponding compatibility of truncations and their natural maps. The natural-transformation and composition assertions of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] imply that the two truncation comparisons obtained by extending the field satisfy the same characterizing equations and coincide. The same holds for their composite defining $\mathcal H^j$. Thus every map and equality at $\Qlb$ is represented at a common finite field and is unchanged upon further extension. No compatibility of arbitrarily chosen splittings is needed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14; common-stage functor convention; uniqueness of truncation comparisons

proof.text:
Finally let $\bar x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be as in the statement. This is a morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, so apply Step 9 to it. Sections on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact and commute with cohomology by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. The functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is, at $E$, exactly sections followed by tensor with $E$ as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Tensor with $E=R[1/\pi]$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies its cohomology with the fibre of the integral cohomology, and the same remains true after rationalization: [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] identifies rational truncations with localized integral truncations. Combining this with the pullback/cohomology comparison gives
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal H^jK)\cong H^j(\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*K)).$$
If $K=\mathcal F$ is in the heart, $L\bar x^*\mathcal F$ is in the point heart and the same exact functors put its fibre in degree zero. At $\Qlb$ apply this at a common finite field; [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] provides the fibre scalar comparisons with their identity and composition compatibility. Together with Step 10 these give exactly the final scalar-extension clause.
